The business manager reported coronavirus-related expenses, and the finance committee report noted support for the proposed budget.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 4-0, with the chair abstaining, to move high school graduation from June 6 to August 1.
The committee approved two line-item transfers 5-0, covering an accreditation stipend, extra clerk hours, projects and early custodial supply purchases.
The committee accepted the coronavirus-related expenditure report 5-0; the business manager is to give further updates in June, July and August.
The Finance Committee report said it supported the proposed school budget, and a member suggested deferring capital items funded by free cash.
The committee accepted the personnel report 5-0 and set its next meeting for May 20.

why_it_matters: Families of seniors now have a new graduation date, and the district is tracking virus-related costs, some of which may be reimbursed by FEMA or state and federal food programs rather than paid from the local budget.

Buying custodial supplies early moves a cost into this year and frees next year's funds for virus-related purchases, and the Finance Committee's remark about deferring free-cash capital items bears on what Town Meeting may be asked to fund.
